outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to LLMs in Tabular Learning
outline.description: This chapter introduces the landscape of tabular data learning, the rise of Large Language Models (LLMs), and the specific gap this textbook addresses. It explores why current LLM-based tabular methods struggle with scalability, cost, and accessibility, setting the stage for the FeatLLM solution.
subtopics: Fundamentals of Tabular Data vs. Textual Data
The Promise of Few-Shot Learning in Real-World Applications
Overview of Large Language Models (LLMs): Capabilities and Limitations
Existing Approaches to LLM-Based Tabular Learning (Serialization & Fine-Tuning)
Critical Analysis of Current Bottlenecks: Inference Cost, Prompt Limits, and API Restrictions
Introducing the Core Philosophy: From End-to-End Prediction to Feature Engineering

outline.description: A deep dive into the conceptual design of FeatLLM. This chapter explains how the framework repurposes LLMs not as predictors, but as intelligent feature engineers that derive human-readable rules to transform raw tabular data into a format suitable for simple statistical models.
subtopics: Core Concept: Rule Extraction as Feature Generation
Workflow Overview: From Raw Data to Simple Linear Classification
The Role of In-Context Learning in Zero-Fine-Tuning Scenarios
Decomposing the Task: Understanding Relationships before Deriving Rules
Advantages Over Traditional Methods: Latency Reduction and Interpretability

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Prompt Engineering for Structured Reasoning
outline.description: This chapter breaks down the intricate prompt design required to coax high-quality rules from an LLM. It covers the three-stage prompting strategy that guides the model through prior knowledge activation, causal reasoning, and strict structural compliance.
subtopics: Component I: Basic Information Description (Task Definition & Feature Context)
Data Serialization Techniques for Tabular Inputs
Component II: Two-Step Reasoning Instruction (Prior Knowledge vs. Evidence Integration)
